comments.author: @osuf3581
comments.text: The problem with a lot of videos like this is that they cheat and basically just learn fixed button patterns. Since they do not make use of proper reinforcement-learning techniques to randomize the environment, the agents do not so much learn to navigate to a pokemon center to heal but that "left left left up left up" gives a high score. It is very different from actual reinforcement learning. Which would be interesting to see, while this is a bit more like a search algorithm.

comments.author: @LunaProtege
comments.text:
I want to suggest, instead of a threshold for the exploration reward; you give fractional rewards. If 1 is "no pixels are the same, completely unique", a reward of 1 is given, but if only a tenth of them are unique, it gives a reward of 0.1; so reward scales from difference.
Edit: also, unique coordinates might be a better thing to scale rewards off of if you're aiming for navigation... But that would likely require some more re-jigging.
